For each temperature reading, update the internal temperature, use the internal helper to find the optimal speed, adjust the internal rotation speed towards it, and calculate the yield efficiency with the other helper. Return a list of yield efficiencies for each batch.

title: Glass Annealing Lehr
spec: Write a class to control a glass annealing lehr tunnel. It manages private variables for the zone temperature, glass stress level, and belt speed. It relies on internal helper methods to calculate the cooling rate based on belt speed, and to determine the residual stress relieved in the current zone based on the cooling rate. The entry function `anneal(speeds)` takes a list of belt speed settings for successive zones. For each zone, update the internal belt speed, calculate the cooling rate using the internal method, and update the internal glass stress level by subtracting the relieved stress calculated by the second helper. Return a list of residual stress levels as the glass exits each zone.

title: Seed Germination Chamber
spec: Design a class for a seed germination chamber. It maintains private state for the light status, internal moisture level, and accumulated degree days. It provides internal helper functions to calculate the daily degree days from the average temperature, and to determine if a watering cycle is needed based on the moisture level dropping below 40 percent. The entry function `germinate(temperatures)` takes a list of average daily temperatures. For each day, use the internal helper to add to the accumulated degree days, decrease the internal moisture slightly, check if watering is required using the second helper, and restore internal moisture if true. Return a list of accumulated degree days for each day.

title: Smokehouse Burner Controller
spec: Implement a class for an automated smokehouse. It keeps private variables for the internal meat temperature, smoke density, and wood chip hopper level. It features private helper methods to calculate the required burner intensity based on the meat temperature deficit, and to determine wood chip consumption based on the burner intensity and target smoke density. The entry function `smoke(readings)` accepts a list of current meat temperature readings over time. For each reading, update internal state, compute the burner intensity using the internal method, and reduce the internal hopper level by the consumption amount calculated by the other helper method. Return a list of remaining wood chip hopper levels.

title: Snowmaking Gun Controller
spec: Build a class to operate a resort snowmaking gun. It stores private state for water pressure, air pressure, and nozzle freezing risk. It requires internal helper methods to calculate the wet bulb temperature from ambient conditions, and to determine the optimal water to air ratio based on the wet bulb temperature. The entry function `snow(conditions)` takes a list of tuples containing ambient temperature and humidity. For each reading, use the internal method to find the wet bulb temperature, compute the optimal pressure ratio with the second helper, and adjust the internal water and air pressures to match this ratio. Return a list of tuples containing the adjusted water and air pressures.

title: Scuba Rebreather Monitor
spec: Create a class for a closed circuit scuba rebreather monitor. It tracks private variables for the oxygen partial pressure, diluent gas remaining, and scrubber efficiency. It includes internal helper methods to calculate the oxygen consumption rate based on depth, and to determine if a diluent flush is necessary when oxygen partial pressure spikes above 1.6 atmospheres. The entry function `monitor(depths)` accepts a list of depth readings in meters. For each reading, calculate oxygen consumption using the internal helper, update the internal oxygen partial pressure, and check if a flush is needed with the second helper, which consumes internal diluent gas and normalizes oxygen. Return a list of boolean values indicating whether a flush occurred for each reading.

title: Anesthesia Vaporizer Controller
spec: Write a class representing a medical anesthesia vaporizer. It manages private state for the liquid anesthetic volume, carrier gas flow rate, and patient weight. It uses private helper functions to calculate the required anesthetic concentration based on the patient weight, and to compute the evaporation rate based on the carrier gas flow and required concentration. The entry function `vaporize(flows)` takes a list of carrier gas flow rates adjusted by an anesthesiologist. For each adjustment, update the internal flow rate, determine the target concentration with the internal helper, calculate the liquid evaporated using the second helper, and deduct it from the internal volume. Return a list of remaining liquid volumes.

title: Neon Glass Bending Tracker
spec: Design a class that tracks the state of glass tubing for neon sign bending. It keeps private variables for the glass temperature, current bend angle, and internal gas pressure. It provides internal helper methods to calculate the pliability score from the glass temperature, and to determine the pressure loss per degree of bending. The entry function `bend(actions)` accepts a list of tuples containing a heating duration in seconds and a bend angle increment. For each action, increase internal temperature based on heating duration, calculate pliability with the internal helper, increment the internal bend angle if pliability is sufficient, and deduct pressure using the second helper. Return a list of current bend angles after each action.

title: Bounding Box Merger
spec: Implement a function `cluster(boxes)` that takes a list of four-element tuples representing the left, top, right, and bottom coordinates of text bounding boxes. The logic must find all boxes that overlap or are separated by a distance less than ten units in either dimension and combine them into a single larger bounding box enclosing all members. The process must repeat until no more boxes can be merged. Return a list of the final merged bounding box tuples sorted by their top coordinate. For example, giving a box from zero to ten and another from twelve to twenty should merge them into a single box from zero to twenty.

title: Knitting Pattern Expander
spec: Provide an entry point `expand(pattern)` that processes a string of knitting instructions consisting of plain stitches, purl stitches, and groups of stitches enclosed in parentheses followed by a multiplier. The logic must parse the string, recursively multiplying any bracketed sequences by their associated number. Track the current row length to ensure it never exceeds one hundred stitches, raising an error if it does. Output a flat list of individual stitch strings representing the full expanded row. For example, passing a purl and a group of two plain stitches multiplied by three should yield a list with one purl and six plain stitches.

title: Geocaching Route Planner
spec: Create a function `plan(caches)` that calculates an optimal sequence of visits to hidden locations represented as a list of coordinate tuples. The algorithm must start at the origin and repeatedly select the closest unvisited location until ten locations are visited or the list is exhausted. It must maintain a running total of the distance traveled, adding a fixed penalty distance of five units each time an elevation change occurs between consecutive points. Return a tuple containing the ordered list of visited coordinates and the total calculated distance. Passing three points in a straight line should return those points in order with their geometric distance.

title: Boarding Pass Parser
spec: Write a function `decode(strip)` that interprets a long string of alphanumeric characters representing a flight boarding pass. The logic must read the first two characters to determine the airline, the next four for the flight number, and then scan forward to locate a slash character dividing the passenger name fields. It must validate that the total length of the strip is exactly sixty characters, padding with spaces if necessary before processing. Output a tuple containing the airline, flight number as an integer, and the formatted passenger name. A sample string starting with two letters and four numbers followed by a name should extract those exact components.

title: Tape Recorder Simulator
spec: Develop a function `simulate(commands)` that tracks the state of a magnetic tape machine given a sequence of action strings like play, record, rewind, and stop. The tape has a maximum capacity of ninety units, and the logic must track the current spool position and the content recorded on the tape as a list of strings. Fast forwarding or rewinding moves the position by ten units per command, while playing or recording moves it by one unit per word. Return a list of strings representing the audio played back during any play commands. For example, recording three words and rewinding followed by play should output those three words.

title: Aquarium Filter Simulator
spec: Implement an entry function `filter(hours)` that models water quality in a fish tank over time. The tank starts with high levels of ammonia, nitrites, and particulate matter. The logic must step through each hour, first passing the water through a mechanical sponge that removes ten percent of particulates, then a biological medium that converts twenty percent of ammonia to nitrites and fifteen percent of nitrites to nitrates. The system must also add a small constant amount of new ammonia every hour to simulate fish waste. Return a list of three numbers representing the final concentrations of ammonia, nitrites, and nitrates. Simulating five hours should show decreased ammonia and increased nitrates.

title: Embroidery Stitch Generator
spec: Create a function `fill(outline)` that converts a list of boundary coordinate tuples into a dense sequence of zig-zag filling stitches. The logic must determine the bounding box of the shape and scan horizontally across it in steps of two units, calculating the intersections of the horizontal scan lines with the outline segments. It must generate a list of alternating left and right coordinate tuples to form a continuous zig-zag path filling the interior of the shape. Return the final list of stitch coordinates. Passing a simple square should result in a list of points alternating back and forth across its width from top to bottom.

title: Origami Crease Simulator
spec: Write a function `fold(instructions)` that models folding a square piece of paper originally spanning from zero to one hundred in both dimensions. The instructions are a list of tuples detailing a fold line starting and ending coordinates, along with a direction. The logic must mirror all current paper boundary vertices across the fold line, discarding the original points on the folded side to simulate layers stacking. After applying all folds, compute the bounding box of the resulting polygon. Output a tuple of the final width and height of the folded shape. Folding the paper exactly in half once should return a width of fifty and a height of one hundred.

title: Gear Ratio Calculator
spec: Implement `calculate(gears)` to determine the final rotation speed and direction of a clockwork mechanism. The input is a list of integers representing the number of teeth on consecutive meshed gears. The logic must iterate through the gears, maintaining the current rotational velocity and tracking the reversal of direction with each mesh. It must also handle compound gears if represented by a nested tuple of two integers, meaning they share an axle and rotate at the same speed. Return a tuple with the final gear speed as a float and an integer representing direction. Passing a ten tooth gear driving a twenty tooth gear should output half the speed in the opposite direction.

title: Sundial Shadow Projector
spec: Provide a function `cast(parameters)` that takes a tuple of latitude, day of the year, and a list of hours. The logic must calculate the sun declination angle based on the day of the year, then for each hour compute the solar altitude and azimuth angles. It must use these angles to determine the length and compass bearing of a shadow cast by a vertical stick of length ten units on a flat horizontal surface. If the sun is below the horizon, the shadow length should be recorded as zero. Return a list of tuples containing the shadow length and bearing for each hour. Midday in summer should yield a short shadow pointing north or south depending on the hemisphere.

title: Harp Pedal Adjuster
spec: Create `pluck(sequence)` to determine the exact musical notes produced by a concert harp. The harp has seven pedals corresponding to the notes of the scale, each able to be set to flat, natural, or sharp positions. The logic must maintain the state of all seven pedals and parse a sequence of commands that either change a specific pedal position or pluck a specific string. When a string is plucked, the system must apply the current pedal modifier for that note to determine the final pitch. Return a list of the modified notes played. Changing the first pedal to sharp and plucking the first string should output the sharp version of that note.

title: Braille Embosser
spec: Develop a function `emboss(text)` that translates standard characters into a layout of braille cells on a grid. The logic must parse the text, inserting a special capital indicator cell before any uppercase letters and converting numbers into a number sign cell followed by the corresponding letter cells. It must maintain a line position and automatically wrap to a new line when the horizontal limit of thirty cells is reached. Return a list of strings where each string represents a row of braille cells using a six-character binary string format for each cell. A short sentence should translate into a matching sequence of dot patterns correctly wrapped.

title: Morse Code Blinker
spec: Write an entry function `flash(message)` that converts a text string into a sequence of timing durations for a signaling lamp. The logic must map each letter to its dot and dash equivalent, then convert these into on and off time values. A dot is one time unit on, a dash is three units on, the space between parts of the same letter is one unit off, between letters is three units off, and between words is seven units off. The system must filter out unsupported punctuation before translation. Return a list of integers where positive numbers indicate duration on and negative numbers indicate duration off. The word hi should produce short positive and negative pulses separated by appropriate gaps.

title: Vinyl Groove Spacer
spec: Implement a function `cut(audio)` that calculates the radial distance of a spiral groove from the center of a record over time. The input is a list of amplitude values representing the sound volume. The logic must start at an outer radius and slowly decrease the radius with each step, increasing the step size when the amplitude is high to prevent adjacent grooves from overlapping, and keeping a minimum step size during quiet parts. It must keep track of the total rotation angle and the remaining disc space, stopping if the center label radius is reached. Return a list of radius values for each full rotation. High amplitudes should result in fewer total rotations fitting on the disc.

title: Typewriter Simulator
spec: Provide an entry point `type(keystrokes)` to process a list of character commands including normal letters, spaces, backspaces, and line feeds. The logic must maintain a virtual paper grid, tracking the current row and column of the print head. A backspace decreases the column without erasing, allowing subsequent characters to overstrike the existing ones by appending them to the grid cell. A line feed advances the row and resets the column to zero. Return a list of strings representing the final printed lines, where overstruck characters are joined together in brackets. Typing a letter, a backspace, and a different letter should yield a single position containing both letters.

title: Hot Air Balloon Controller
spec: Create a function `fly(actions)` that simulates the vertical motion of a hot air balloon given a sequence of burner blasts and vent openings. The logic must maintain internal variables for envelope temperature, ambient temperature, vertical velocity, and altitude. Burner blasts increase the envelope temperature, which generates upward buoyant acceleration, while the envelope constantly cools over time toward ambient. Venting rapidly decreases the temperature. The system must update the velocity and altitude step by step, preventing altitude from dropping below ground level. Output the maximum altitude reached during the flight. A series of long blasts should result in a high peak altitude.

title: Lighthouse Flasher
spec: Write `rotate(panels)` to model the light signature of a lighthouse seen by a distant observer. The input is a list of lens panel types that make up a circular rotating assembly, where each panel can be a bullseye lens, a colored glass pane, or a blank plate. The logic must step through time as the assembly rotates at a fixed speed, calculating when a lens sweeps past the observer line of sight to produce a bright flash, or when a colored pane changes the light hue. It must maintain the rotational angle and map it to the observer bearing. Return a list of flash events with their exact time and color. A bullseye followed by a red pane should output a white flash then a steady red light.

title: Film Projector Drive
spec: Implement `crank(milliseconds)` to trace the state of a movie projector mechanism over a given duration. The mechanism consists of a continuously rotating drive pin that engages a slotted wheel to pull the film down one frame at a time, while a rotary shutter blocks the light during the pull-down phase. The logic must calculate the angular position of the drive pin for every millisecond, determining whether the slotted wheel is stationary or moving. It must synchronize the shutter position to ensure the light is only open when the film is completely still. Return the total number of frames successfully projected. Running for one second at standard speed should output twenty four frames.

title: Sonar Echo Simulator
spec: Provide a function `sound(obstacles)` that processes a list of underwater target distances and their relative sizes. The logic must simulate a sonar pulse traveling outward at a constant speed of sound, tracking the time it takes to reach each obstacle and bounce back. It must calculate the strength of the returning echo, which degrades based on the total distance traveled and the size of the target. The system must sort the returning echoes by their arrival time and filter out any that fall below a minimum detectable threshold. Return a list of tuples containing the arrival time and echo strength. A large close target should yield a quick, strong return.

title: Kite Tension Simulator
spec: Develop an entry function `test(gusts)` that models the mechanical stress on a kite string during a windy day. The input is a sequence of wind speed values over time. The logic must track the current altitude and angle of the kite, which increase when wind speed rises and decrease during lulls. It must calculate the aerodynamic drag and lift forces at each time step, translating these into tension on the string based on its length and the kite surface area. The system must record the tension at each step and snap the string if it exceeds a critical limit. Return the highest tension recorded before the simulation ends or the string breaks. A sudden massive gust should return the breaking strain limit.

title: Boomerang Flight Simulator
spec: Create a function `throw(parameters)` that calculates the returning path of a boomerang based on initial velocity, spin rate, and wind speed. The logic must simulate the flight in discrete time steps, tracking the two dimensional coordinates, heading, and remaining rotational energy. It must apply an aerodynamic turning force that curves the heading proportionately to the current spin rate and velocity, while gradually reducing the velocity and spin due to drag. The simulation stops when the altitude hits zero. Return a list of the coordinates at each step. A proper set of inputs should produce a list of points that trace a circular path back towards the origin.

title: Yo-yo State Tracker
spec: Write an entry point `play(moves)` to track the physical state of a yo-yo during a string trick routine. The yo-yo has properties for spin speed, string wrap length, and mount state. The logic must process commands like throw, bind, mount, and dismount. A throw unwinds the string and starts the spin; a mount adds a layer of friction that slowly decreases spin speed; a bind rewinds the string only if the spin is sufficiently high. The system must validate that moves are possible from the current state, raising an error if a bind is attempted while the yo-yo is stationary. Output a string describing the final state, such as spinning on string or returned to hand.

title: Abacus Simulator
spec: Implement a function `compute(operations)` that simulates adding and subtracting numbers on a traditional bead abacus. The logic must represent the abacus as a series of columns, each tracking the position of one upper bead and four lower beads. To add or subtract, the system must parse the input numbers digit by digit, moving the required beads in each column. It must handle carry-over and borrow operations naturally by shifting beads in the adjacent higher column when a lower column overflows or underflows. After processing all operations, read the final positions of the beads. Return the resulting total as an integer. Adding five and seven should trigger a carry and result in twelve.

title: Pinball Bumper Simulator
spec: Provide an entry `launch(actions)` that tracks a ball traversing a pinball table. The table contains several stationary circular bumpers and two flippers at the bottom. The logic must update the ball position and velocity in small time steps, applying a constant downward acceleration for gravity. It must detect collisions with bumpers, which reflect the ball and add a fixed velocity boost. The input actions specify exact times when the left or right flipper is activated, which will strike the ball upward if it is within their hit zones. Return the total number of bumper hits before the ball falls below the bottom of the table. Good flipper timing should keep the ball in play and accumulate multiple hits.

title: Fountain Choreography
spec: Create `spray(sequence)` to model the arcs of water droplets shot from a programmable fountain nozzle. The input sequence defines changes to the nozzle tilt angle and water pressure at specific times. The logic must simulate the emission of a water droplet every tenth of a second, assigning it an initial velocity vector based on the current angle and pressure. It must track the parabolic trajectory of every droplet in the air, applying gravity until it hits the ground. The system must record the maximum height achieved by any droplet and the furthest horizontal distance reached. Output a tuple of these two maximum values. A high pressure vertical shot should maximize height but have zero horizontal distance.

title: Potion Brewing Cauldron
spec: The entry function `brew(ingredients)` takes a list of strings representing ingredients added one by one. The cauldron starts with zero volume, a temperature of twenty degrees, and zero toxicity. Adding fireweed increases volume by one and temperature by fifty. Adding icecap increases volume by one and decreases temperature by twenty. Adding snake venom increases volume by one and toxicity by five. If the temperature goes above one hundred degrees, the liquid boils and volume decreases by one, while toxicity increases by two. If temperature drops below zero, it freezes and toxicity resets to zero. The function returns a list of three numbers representing final volume, temperature, and toxicity. Example: ['fireweed', 'fireweed', 'icecap'] returns [3, 100, 2].

title: Photographic Film Developer
spec: The entry function `develop(steps)` takes a list of numbers representing minutes spent in the chemical bath. The bath starts with a concentration of one hundred percent and a temperature of twenty degrees. Each minute spent in the bath reduces concentration by two percent. If the bath temperature is below twenty five, it naturally warms up by one degree per minute of use. If the concentration drops below fifty percent, development becomes uneven and a quality penalty score increases by one for every subsequent minute used. If a step is zero minutes, the bath rests and cools down by two degrees without losing concentration. Returns the final quality penalty score. Example: [30, 5] returns 5.

title: Steam Engine Governor
spec: The entry function `govern(pressures)` takes a list of numbers representing furnace heat levels applied per cycle. The engine starts with zero steam pressure, a valve position of zero, and zero speed. Each heat level adds to the steam pressure. If pressure exceeds one hundred, the governor automatically opens the valve by adding ten to its position, which vents twenty units of pressure immediately. The engine speed increases by the current pressure minus the valve position. If speed exceeds five hundred, an overspeed warning counter increments, and the valve opens completely to fifty, venting all pressure to zero. Returns a tuple of final speed and the warning count. Example: [50, 80, 90] returns (130, 0).

title: Hot Tub Controller
spec: The entry function `regulate(events)` takes a list of strings such as enter, leave, heat, or cool. The tub starts empty of users, with the pump off, and a water temperature of thirty degrees. When a user enters, the pump turns on automatically and temperature drops by one degree. When a user leaves, if no users remain, the pump turns off. The heat command increases temperature by five degrees. If the pump is off, the heat command cannot increase the temperature above thirty five degrees for safety. The cool command drops the temperature by two degrees. Returns a tuple of the final temperature and pump status as a boolean. Example: ['enter', 'heat', 'heat'] returns (40, True).

title: Ice Cream Churner
spec: The entry function `churn(actions)` takes a list of strings representing actions. Start with a viscosity of zero, a drum temperature of zero, and motor speed of ten. The action freeze lowers temperature by five. The action spin increases viscosity by two if temperature is below negative ten, otherwise viscosity drops by one. The action thicken increases motor speed by five but warms the drum by two degrees. If motor speed goes over twenty and viscosity is above ten, the motor overheats and speed drops to zero. Return a tuple of final viscosity and motor speed. Example: ['freeze', 'freeze', 'freeze', 'spin', 'spin', 'thicken'] returns (4, 15).

title: Printing Press Ink Controller
spec: The entry function `press(pages)` takes a list of numbers representing the color density of each page. Starts with an ink reservoir of one thousand, roller speed of zero, and a page count of zero. Each page printed consumes ink equal to its color density. The roller speed increases by one for each page. If the roller speed reaches ten, friction heats the ink, evaporating five extra units of ink per page. If the reservoir drops below two hundred, the press enters eco mode, halving the ink consumed per page rounded down. Returns a tuple of the remaining ink and final roller speed. Example: [100, 100, 100] returns (700, 3).

title: Paintball Marker Firing Mechanism
spec: The entry function `fire(triggers)` takes a list of booleans where true means a trigger pull. Starts with a gas pressure of three thousand, hopper count of two hundred, and barrel heat of zero. Each true trigger pull consumes one paintball from the hopper and fifty units of gas pressure, while increasing barrel heat by five. If pressure drops below one thousand, a trigger pull consumes no paintballs and only vents ten pressure. If barrel heat exceeds fifty, the marker jams and ignores the next two trigger pulls, while cooling down by twenty degrees per ignored pull. Returns a tuple of remaining paintballs and pressure. Example: [True, True, True] returns (197, 2850).

title: Cotton Candy Machine
spec: The entry function `spin(sugar)` takes a list of numbers representing grams of sugar added per minute. Starts with spinner heat at zero, sugar reserve at zero, and total fluff produced at zero. Each minute, the added sugar goes into the reserve. Then, spinner heat increases by ten. If spinner heat is at least fifty, the machine converts up to twenty grams of sugar reserve into total fluff, cooling the spinner by five for every ten grams converted. If heat reaches one hundred, the sugar burns, emptying the reserve and dropping heat to zero. Returns the total fluff produced. Example: [30, 30, 30, 30, 30] returns 80.

title: Perfume Distillation Still
spec: The entry function `distill(hours)` takes a list of numbers representing the duration of heating phases in hours. Starts with a boiler pressure of ten, temperature of ninety, and residue buildup of zero. Each hour of heating decreases pressure by one and temperature by one. Between phases, the still rests and recovers for ten hours, increasing pressure by five and temperature by five, up to a maximum of fifteen and ninety five respectively. However, every hour heated adds one to residue buildup. If residue buildup exceeds five, recovery only adds two to pressure and temperature instead of five. Returns a tuple of final pressure and temperature. Example: [5, 5] returns (15, 95).

title: Microscope Stage Calibrator
spec: The entry function `calibrate(movements)` takes a list of strings representing directional nudges like up, down, left, right. Starts with horizontal position zero, vertical position zero, and tracking rate of one. Up increases vertical position by the tracking rate, down decreases it. Right increases horizontal position by the tracking rate, left decreases it. If three consecutive horizontal movements occur in the same direction, the tracking rate doubles. A movement in a new direction resets the tracking rate to one. If vertical position exceeds ninety, it gets capped at ninety. Returns a tuple of the horizontal and vertical positions. Example: ['up', 'up', 'right'] returns (1, 2).

title: Water Purification Reverse Osmosis
spec: The entry function `purify(cycles)` takes a list of numbers representing liters of source water to process per cycle. Starts with a membrane health of one hundred, filter capacity of five hundred, and pure water tank at zero. Processing each liter uses one unit of filter capacity and yields half a liter of pure water. If filter capacity reaches zero, processing continues but membrane health drops by one per liter processed, and the yield drops to a quarter liter. If membrane health drops below fifty, the system halts and processes no more water. Returns a tuple of pure water tank volume and membrane health. Example: [100, 100] returns (100.0, 100).

title: Metal Detector Discriminator
spec: The entry function `sweep(signals)` takes a list of numbers representing magnetic signal strengths. Starts with a base threshold of fifty, battery level of one hundred, and a count of found targets at zero. Each signal costs one battery level. If a signal is above the threshold, it is considered a target and added to the count. If three signals in a row are below the threshold, the device assumes heavy mineralization and raises the threshold by ten to compensate. If battery drops below twenty, the device lowers its scanning power, halving all incoming signal strengths before checking against the threshold. Returns the number of found targets. Example: [60, 40, 30, 20, 70] returns 1.

title: Hovercraft Lift Fan
spec: The entry function `hover(commands)` takes a list of strings representing throttle commands up, down, or coast. Starts with fan speed zero, skirt pressure zero, and battery at one hundred. Throttle up increases fan speed by ten and consumes five battery. Throttle down decreases fan speed by ten and consumes two battery. Coast does not change speed but consumes one battery. Skirt pressure always becomes equal to half the fan speed. If skirt pressure goes above forty, a relief valve opens, dropping fan speed by twenty instantly to prevent damage. If battery reaches zero, speed goes to zero. Returns a tuple of final fan speed and skirt pressure. Example: ['up', 'up', 'up'] returns (30, 15).

title: Tank Turret Traverse Motor
spec: The entry function `traverse(commands)` takes a list of strings: elevate, depress, rotate, lock. Starts with elevation zero, angle zero, locked status zero, and hydraulic pressure at fifty. Elevate increases elevation by ten, up to a max of fifty. Depress decreases elevation by ten, minimum zero. Rotate increases angle by ninety degrees, wrapping around at three hundred sixty. Lock sets the locked status to one. Any action uses one hydraulic pressure. If pressure is below ten, the motor enters low power mode where elevate and depress only change elevation by five. You can only rotate if elevation is at least twenty and locked status is zero. Returns a tuple of elevation, angle, and hydraulic pressure. Example: ['elevate', 'elevate', 'rotate', 'lock'] returns (20, 90, 46).

title: Drawbridge Winch Controller
spec: The entry function `operate(signals)` takes a list of strings: open, close, lock, unlock. Starts with angle zero, locked status true, and tension zero. An open signal increases the angle by fifteen degrees, but only if the bridge is unlocked. A close signal decreases the angle by fifteen degrees, minimum zero. If an open signal is received while locked, the angle does not change but cable tension increases by ten. If tension exceeds twenty, the winch jams and ignores all future open and close signals until a maintenance reset which happens automatically after three ignored signals. Returns a tuple of angle and tension. Example: ['open', 'open', 'unlock', 'open'] returns (15, 20).

title: Suspension Bridge Cable Tuner
spec: The entry function `tune(loads)` takes a list of numbers representing vehicle weights entering the span. Starts with cable stretch zero, tensioner speed ten, and stress alerts zero. Each load adds its weight to the cable stretch. If total stretch exceeds one thousand, the tensioner speed reduces by five to compensate. If the speed drops to zero or below, a stress alert is recorded, and the system automatically rejects the last added load, restoring the stretch and resetting speed to five. Returns a tuple of total stretch and stress alerts. Example: [500, 600, 200] returns (1100, 1).

title: Rock Tumbler Polisher
spec: The entry function `tumble(days)` takes a list of numbers representing hours run per day. Starts with grit stage one, drum speed thirty, and rock smoothness zero. Each hour run adds one to rock smoothness. At the end of each day, if the daily hours exceeded ten, the drum speed drops by two due to belt wear. When rock smoothness reaches fifty, the grit stage automatically advances by one and smoothness resets to zero. If the grit stage reaches four, the tumbler is done and any further hours have no effect. Returns a tuple of final grit stage and drum speed. Example: [12, 12, 12, 12, 12] returns (2, 20).

title: Tobacco Leaf Curing Barn
spec: The entry function `cure(readings)` takes a list of numbers representing ambient humidity readings every hour. Starts with leaf moisture fifty, heater power zero, and venting status false. If humidity is above sixty, heater power increases by ten, up to a maximum of one hundred. If humidity is below forty, venting status becomes true, otherwise false. Each hour, leaf moisture drops by an amount equal to the heater power divided by twenty. If venting is true, leaf moisture drops by an additional two units. If moisture drops below ten, the curing is complete and moisture stays at ten. Returns a tuple of final moisture and heater power. Example: [70, 70] returns (48.5, 20).

title: Electric Scooter Battery Manager
spec: The entry function `ride(demands)` takes a list of numbers representing power demands per minute. Starts with battery capacity one thousand, temperature twenty, and eco mode false. Each minute, the demand is subtracted from capacity. If demand is over fifty, temperature increases by five. If temperature exceeds forty, eco mode engages. While in eco mode, actual power drawn is capped at thirty, regardless of demand, and temperature drops by two each minute. Eco mode turns off when temperature falls below thirty. Returns a tuple of remaining capacity and final temperature. Example: [60, 60, 60, 60, 60] returns (740, 45).

title: Popcorn Popper Temperature Tracker
spec: The entry function `pop(intervals)` takes a list of numbers representing seconds the heating element is on. Starts with kettle heat twenty, kernel count one hundred, and popped volume zero. For each interval, kettle heat increases by the number of seconds. Once kettle heat exceeds one hundred, every ten additional units of heat pops five kernels, turning them into fifty units of popped volume, and removing them from the kernel count. If kettle heat goes above two hundred, any remaining kernels burn, kernel count becomes zero, and no more popped volume can be created. Returns a tuple of popped volume and remaining kernels. Example: [90, 20] returns (150, 85).

title: Wave Pool Generator
spec: The entry function `surge(pulses)` takes a list of numbers representing pump activation durations. Starts with flow rate zero, motor wear zero, and a synchronized mode set to false. Each pulse adds its duration to the flow rate. If a pulse is exactly five, it is considered a perfect rhythm and switches the system to synchronized mode. In synchronized mode, every pulse adds double its duration to the flow rate. However, any pulse longer than ten increases motor wear by one. If motor wear reaches three, the system forces a shutdown, zeroing the flow rate and exiting synchronized mode. Returns a tuple of flow rate and motor wear. Example: [5, 6, 11] returns (39, 1).

title: Fog Machine Fluid Pump
spec: The entry function `fog(cues)` takes a list of strings: blast, trickle, wait. Starts with fluid level five hundred, heater temp two hundred, and a clogged state false. A blast consumes fifty fluid and drops heater temp by twenty. A trickle consumes ten fluid and drops temp by five. A wait consumes no fluid and raises temp by thirty, up to a max of two hundred. If heater temp drops below one hundred, the machine cannot vaporize fluid, causing it to clog; the clogged state becomes true. Once clogged, blasts and trickles consume no fluid and only lower temp by five until a wait clears the clog by heating back above one hundred fifty. Returns a tuple of fluid level and clogged state. Example: ['blast', 'blast', 'blast', 'blast', 'blast', 'blast'] returns (200, True).

title: Arcade Ticket Shredder
spec: The entry function `shred(tickets)` takes a list of numbers representing ticket lengths inserted. Starts with bin capacity two hundred, points awarded zero, and a jammed state false. A value of twenty five represents a standard ticket. If a standard ticket is inserted, points awarded goes up by twenty five, capacity drops by one. If a ticket of length ten is inserted, the shredder becomes jammed. While jammed, all tickets are rejected and do not increase points or use capacity. A length of fifty represents a clearing tool, which un-jams the shredder and removes fifty from points awarded as a penalty. Returns a tuple of remaining capacity and total points. Example: [25, 10, 25, 50, 25] returns (198, 0).

title: Automatic Dog Ball Launcher
spec: The entry function `launch(distances)` takes a list of numbers representing the desired throw distance in meters. Starts with spring tension zero, balls loaded five, and battery one hundred. To throw, the spring tension increases to match the desired distance, consuming battery equal to half the distance. If battery is too low to reach the desired distance, it uses all remaining battery and sets the tension to double that amount. Once tension is set, one ball is subtracted from loaded, and tension resets to zero. If zero balls are loaded, the machine ignores the command and beeps, consuming one battery. Returns a tuple of balls loaded and remaining battery. Example: [40, 40, 40] returns (2, 40).

title: Treadmill Motor Controller
spec: The entry function `run(adjustments)` takes a list of strings: faster, slower, higher, lower. Starts with belt speed zero, incline zero, and total calories zero. Faster increases belt speed by two, max twelve. Slower decreases belt speed by two, min zero. Higher increases incline by one, max fifteen. Lower decreases incline by one, min zero. For every command processed, total calories burned increases by the current belt speed plus half the current incline. If belt speed is zero, no calories are burned regardless of incline. Returns a tuple of belt speed, incline, and calories. Example: ['faster', 'higher', 'faster', 'slower'] returns (2, 1, 11.5).

title: Vintage Cipher Machine
spec: Write a main function `encrypt(rotors)` that instantiates a custom class to simulate a rotor based substitution cipher. The class must maintain internal state for three spinning wheels. When the function passes a message to the class, the class should process it character by character, utilizing internal helper methods to increment the wheel positions, map the letter forward through three shifting stages based on the current wheel integers, reflect it using a fixed alphabet reversal, and map it backward. The main function should return the final encrypted phrase.

title: Automated Cocktail Mixer
spec: Create an entry function `mix(requests)` that initializes a drink dispenser class and processes a list of requested drink names. The class must keep internal volume levels for spirit, mixer, and syrup, alongside a boolean flag for cup presence. For each request, the class should rely on hidden routines to verify sufficient liquid inventory, actuate the dispensing valves which deducts the required volumes, and agitate the mixture. The function should return a list of boolean results indicating which requests were successfully fulfilled.

title: Mail Sorting Conveyor
spec: Write a function `sort(weights)` that uses a custom class to model a mail sorting belt. The class must store internal tallies for accepted parcels, rejected parcels, and current motor speed. As the function passes the list of package weights to the class, the class must use private methods to determine if a weight exceeds the fifty unit limit, compute the correct bin destination based on weight categories, and adjust the motor speed downward if heavy items appear consecutively. Return a tuple of final accepted and rejected counts from the class.

title: Paper Mill Pulp Beater
spec: Implement a function `beat(minutes)` that instantiates a pulp processing class to run for a given duration. The class should track internal variables for water percentage, average fiber length, and blade height. During the processing loop, the class must call internal operations to lower the blades by one unit per minute, inject water to maintain a minimum ninety percent moisture level, and chop the fibers which reduces their length based on the current blade height. The function returns the final fiber length.

title: Deep Fryer Oil Vat
spec: Write a function `fry(durations)` that processes a list of cooking times using a custom deep fryer class. The class must maintain internal states for oil temperature, heater activity, accumulated usage time, and basket position. For each cooking time, the class must execute internal steps to preheat the oil to three hundred fifty degrees, lower the basket, increment the usage timer, raise the basket, and disable the heater. If usage exceeds one hundred minutes, a hidden maintenance routine must reset the oil. Return the total elapsed operational time.

title: Observatory Dome Rotator
spec: Create a function `align(azimuths)` that directs a telescope dome class to a series of sky coordinates. The class starts at zero degrees and tracks motor temperature and shutter status internally. For each target, the class must use hidden procedures to calculate the shortest rotational path clockwise or counterclockwise, engage the rotation motor while adding heat for each degree moved, pause to cool if temperature exceeds eighty degrees, and finally open the viewing shutter. The function should return the total operational time taken.

title: Automated Book Binder
spec: Design a function `bind(count)` that manufactures a batch of books by instantiating a binding assembly class. The class holds internal registers for glue temperature, cover stock, and error state. To process the batch, it must execute hidden procedures for each book to heat the glue to optimal viscosity, apply glue to the spine, attach the outer cover while decrementing stock, and verify physical alignment. The function should return the number of successfully bound books before stock ran out or errors occurred.

title: Escalator Motor Drive
spec: Write a function `regulate(loads)` that regulates an escalator class over discrete time steps based on passenger load weights. The class keeps internal variables for step velocity, motor torque, and a consecutive empty step counter. For each load, the class uses internal calculators to apply an acceleration profile for increasing weights, engage a braking routine if weight drops abruptly, and decrement velocity to a crawl if the empty counter exceeds five steps. Return a list of recorded speeds.

title: Antique Clock Pendulum
spec: Implement an entry function `tick(seconds)` that drives a mechanical grandfather clock class for a given duration. The class internally monitors the mainspring tension, the pendulum swing angle, and the time. Each second, it must utilize internal mechanics to release a burst of spring energy, apply air resistance friction to the swing angle, and advance the gears if the swing crosses the center point. A hidden routine should rewind the spring when tension drops below ten. Return the final spring tension.

title: Vinyl Record Press
spec: Write a function `press(weights)` that manufactures records using a custom pressing machine class. The class stores internal parameters for hydraulic pressure, plate heat, and a clamp locking status. For each desired record weight, the class coordinates several hidden phases: a warming phase to bring plates to one hundred sixty degrees, a compression phase that scales hydraulic pressure to the target weight, a holding phase for twenty seconds, and a cooling water injection phase. Return the total manufacturing time for all records.

title: Pottery Wheel Speed Governor
spec: Create a function `spin(pressures)` that models a ceramic throwing session using a motorized wheel class. The class keeps internal state for rotation speed, motor strain, and clay structural integrity. For each pedal pressure input, the wheel must execute internal logic to adjust rotation speed, calculate the centrifugal force pulling on the clay, and apply a stabilizing counter force. If rotation exceeds a dynamically calculated safe threshold, the clay collapses. Return a boolean indicating if the pot survived.

title: Cotton Gin Separator
spec: Design a function `separate(volumes)` that processes batches of raw cotton using a custom separator class. The class maintains internal counters for raw hopper volume, clean lint, discarded seeds, and saw speed. For each batch, the class must invoke internal steps to rev the saw motor, tease the fibers which converts the raw volume into lint and seeds at a fixed ratio, and clear the mesh screens of accumulated debris. Return a tuple containing the total lint and seed counts.

title: Vintage Film Splicer
spec: Write a function `splice(edits)` that cuts and joins cinematic film using a splicer class. The class tracks the current frame index, remaining splicing tape, and cutting blade sharpness internally. For each target edit frame in the sequence, the class uses hidden operations to advance the reel, trigger the guillotine blade to cut which slightly degrades blade sharpness, and apply a strip of joining tape. If tape depletes, it must safely halt operations. Return the total number of successful edits.

title: Submarine Torpedo Tube
spec: Implement a function `launch(commands)` that executes a series of launch instructions using a torpedo tube class. The class holds internal statuses for inner door state, outer door state, tube water level, and equalization pressure. Each launch command must orchestrate strictly ordered internal routines: lock the inner door, flood the chamber, equalize pressure with the ocean depth, open the outer door, and expel the payload. Return a count of how many launches successfully completed all internal stages without aborting.

title: Laser Tag Arena Scorer
spec: Create a function `score(events)` that processes match events using a dedicated arena class. The class maintains internal tracking for player health, points, and base control zones. For each event, the class triggers internal evaluators to confirm the target has remaining health, deduct damage based on the tag location, award points to the attacker, and verify if a base control threshold was reached to award team bonus points. Return a list of the final scores for the two competing teams.

title: Combine Harvester Monitor
spec: Write a function `harvest(yields)` that tracks crop collection using a combine harvester class. The class internally monitors grain tank fill level, threshing drum speed, and separation fan speed. For each crop yield data point, the class must invoke private routines to increase the grain tank volume, adjust the drum speed upward if the yield inflow spikes rapidly, and engage the separation fan to clear excess chaff. Return a tuple of the final collected grain amount and the highest recorded drum speed.

title: Industrial Pasta Extruder
spec: Design a function `extrude(lengths)` that produces noodles using a factory extruder class. The class internally tracks dough viscosity, die temperature, and remaining batch size. For each requested noodle length, the class utilizes internal steps to heat the die to prevent sticking, press the dough through the template which depletes the overall batch size, and trigger the slicing blade once the extruded amount matches the target. Return the total count of successfully sized noodles produced before the dough ran out.

title: Mechanical Loom Weaver
spec: Write an entry function `weave(rows)` that operates an industrial textile weaving machine class. The class internally tracks warp thread tension, shuttle position, and current fabric length. For the given number of rows, the class must coordinate several hidden actions per row: raising the alternate warp threads, firing the horizontal shuttle across the shed, and beating the new thread into place with a reed. Each internal action updates the tension dynamically and adds to the length. Return the final length of the woven cloth.

title: Commercial Dishwasher Controller
spec: Write a class to control a commercial dishwasher. The entry function `wash(commands)` accepts a list of string instructions. The machine tracks internal temperature starting at twenty, detergent level starting at one hundred, current cycle phase starting at idle, and runtime minutes starting at zero. When receiving a heat command, it increases temperature by fifteen degrees up to a maximum of eighty. A wash command consumes twenty units of detergent, increases runtime by ten, and requires the temperature to be at least sixty; if not, it automatically forces a heating phase first. A drain command resets the cycle phase to idle and temperature to twenty. The function should return a tuple of the final temperature, remaining detergent, and total runtime.

title: Deep Space Probe Antenna Aligner
spec: Implement a class to maintain signal lock for a deep space probe. The entry function `align(adjustments)` takes a list of numerical tuples representing target changes in azimuth and elevation. The system tracks current azimuth starting at zero, current elevation starting at zero, signal strength starting at one hundred, and lock status starting as true. For each adjustment, both angles are modified. If the absolute difference between azimuth and elevation exceeds thirty, signal strength drops by ten; otherwise it increases by five up to one hundred. If signal strength falls below fifty, the lock status becomes false and all subsequent adjustments are ignored until a manual recalibrate command string is received, which resets angles to zero and restores signal lock. Return the final azimuth, elevation, and signal strength.

title: Commercial Laundry Washing Machine
spec: Design a class that operates an industrial washing machine. The entry function `launder(events)` processes a list of action strings. The machine maintains internal states for drum speed starting at zero, water level starting at empty, load weight starting at zero, and unbalance detection starting as false. Adding clothes increases load weight; if it exceeds fifty, unbalance detection triggers. A fill command sets water level to full if weight is under fifty, but only to half if an unbalance is detected. A spin command increases drum speed by four hundred if balanced, or by one hundred if unbalanced. A drain command resets water level to empty and drum speed to zero. Return a tuple containing the final drum speed, water level string, and load weight.

title: High Speed Rail Suspension Tuner
spec: Create a class to manage the active suspension of a high speed train. The entry function `tune(readings)` takes a list of integers representing track curvature severities. The system tracks left bogie pressure starting at fifty, right bogie pressure starting at fifty, tilt angle starting at zero, and passenger comfort index starting at one hundred. For each reading, the system leans into the curve: if the reading is positive, left pressure increases by the reading and right pressure decreases by the reading, adjusting the tilt angle proportionally. If the tilt angle exceeds twenty, the comfort index drops by five. The system must automatically rebalance pressures towards fifty after every three readings to prevent permanent list. Return the final left pressure, right pressure, and comfort index.

title: Seawater Desalination Plant Simulator
spec: Write a class simulating a reverse osmosis desalination unit. The entry function `desalinate(operations)` accepts a list of commands. The unit tracks membrane pressure starting at one hundred, salinity output starting at zero, filter health starting at one hundred, and fresh water produced starting at zero. A pump command increases pressure by ten and produces five units of fresh water, but decreases filter health by two. A backwash command reduces pressure by twenty and restores filter health by ten. If filter health drops below fifty, salinity output increases by five for every subsequent pump command. If pressure exceeds one hundred and fifty, the system enters an emergency bypass, preventing any water production until a reset command is issued. Return the total water produced, final filter health, and final salinity.

title: Jet Engine Thrust Reverser
spec: Implement a class to manage a jet engine thrust reverser deployment. The entry function `reverse(telemetry)` processes a list of integers representing airspeed. The system monitors cowl position starting at closed, lock actuator status starting at engaged, engine speed starting at idle, and structural stress starting at zero. To open the cowl, the airspeed must be below one hundred and sixty; if above, structural stress increases by twenty and the cowl remains closed. When a valid speed is encountered, the lock actuator disengages, the cowl position transitions to open, and engine speed ramps up to maximum reverse over the next three telemetry readings. If structural stress reaches one hundred, a fault is triggered, instantly reverting all states to starting values. Return the final cowl position, engine speed, and structural stress.

title: Industrial Wood Chipper Controller
spec: Build a class that controls a heavy duty wood chipper. The function `chip(loads)` receives a list of integers representing the density of incoming wood pieces. The machine tracks drum speed starting at two thousand, hydraulic feed rate starting at ten, engine load starting at zero, and jam status starting as false. For each wood piece, engine load increases by the density and drum speed drops by double the density. If engine load exceeds one hundred, the jam status becomes true, feed rate drops to zero, and the drum speed drops to zero. A reverse command string clears the jam and resets engine load to zero. Whenever drum speed falls below one thousand without jamming, the machine must auto throttle by increasing speed by five hundred. Return the final drum speed, feed rate, and jam status.

title: Milk Pasteurization Vat
spec: Create a class to control a dairy pasteurization process. The entry function `pasteurize(phases)` handles a list of string directives. The vat tracks internal temperature starting at four, agitator speed starting at zero, holding time starting at zero, and pasteurization status starting as incomplete. A heat command increases temperature by twenty and starts the agitator at thirty. A hold command adds ten to holding time; if temperature is exactly seventy two and holding time reaches fifteen, the status becomes complete. If temperature ever exceeds eighty, the milk is scorched, setting holding time to zero and forcing a cool command to lower temperature back to four. Return the final temperature, agitator speed, and a string representing whether pasteurization is complete or incomplete.

title: Automated Car Wash Bay
spec: Write a class governing an automatic drive through car wash. The entry function `wash(sensors)` reads a list of strings representing vehicle positions. The bay tracks conveyor speed starting at zero, soap level starting at two hundred, brush speed starting at zero, and blower intensity starting at zero. When a vehicle enters, conveyor speed becomes five. As it reaches the soap zone, soap level decreases by thirty and brush speed jumps to one hundred. In the rinse zone, brush speed drops to zero. In the dry zone, blower intensity rises to maximum. If a stall string is detected, conveyor speed halts, brushes stop, and blowers turn off for safety until a resume string is read. Return the remaining soap, final conveyor speed, and final blower intensity.

title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Chamber
spec: Develop a class for a medical hyperbaric chamber. The function `treat(commands)` takes a list of string commands. The system tracks atmospheric pressure starting at one, oxygen concentration starting at twenty one, compression rate starting at zero, and patient heart rate starting at eighty. A pressurize command increases pressure by one and compression rate by two; if pressure exceeds three, patient heart rate increases by ten. An enrich command boosts oxygen concentration by ten up to a maximum of one hundred. A decompress command reduces pressure by one, but if oxygen concentration is above fifty during decompression, pressure drops by two instead to prevent toxicity. Return the final pressure, oxygen concentration, and patient heart rate.

title: Electric Vehicle Charging Station
spec: Implement a class for a rapid charging terminal. The entry function `charge(intervals)` accepts a list of integers representing current draw requests. The terminal tracks battery charge level starting at ten, output voltage starting at four hundred, cooling fluid flow starting at zero, and cable temperature starting at twenty. For each request, charge level increases by five and cable temperature rises by the request amount. If cable temperature exceeds fifty, the station must activate cooling, increasing fluid flow by ten and dropping temperature by fifteen. If the charge level reaches eighty, the output voltage drops to two hundred to trickle charge, and any subsequent requests only increase charge level by one. Return the final charge level, output voltage, and cable temperature.

title: Helicopter Rotor Pitch Controller
spec: Create a class managing a helicopter swashplate. The entry function `pitch(inputs)` accepts a list of tuples containing collective and cyclic stick movements. The controller tracks main collective angle starting at ten, lateral cyclic starting at zero, longitudinal cyclic starting at zero, and hydraulic pressure starting at three thousand. Each input alters the respective angles. If the combined absolute change in any step exceeds fifteen, hydraulic pressure drops by two hundred. If pressure falls below two thousand, control response becomes sluggish, and subsequent angle changes are halved. A pump command string restores pressure to three thousand. Return the final collective angle, longitudinal cyclic, and hydraulic pressure.

title: Industrial Plastic Injection Molder
spec: Design a class for an injection molding machine. The entry function `mold(cycles)` takes a list of string commands. The machine tracks barrel temperature starting at two hundred, plastic viscosity starting at high, injection pressure starting at zero, and clamp force starting at zero. A heat command increases temperature by twenty, which changes viscosity to low if temperature exceeds two hundred forty. A clamp command sets clamp force to maximum. An inject command increases pressure to one hundred, but if viscosity is high, pressure spikes to two hundred and triggers a safety abort, resetting clamp force and pressure to zero. A cool command reduces temperature by thirty. Return the final barrel temperature, clamp force, and injection pressure.

title: Commercial Bread Proofer Chamber
spec: Write a class for a bakery proofer. The function `proof(readings)` processes a list of integers representing ambient humidity shifts. The chamber tracks internal humidity starting at sixty, internal temperature starting at thirty, yeast gas concentration starting at zero, and fan speed starting at zero. For each positive shift, humidity increases; for each negative shift, it decreases. If humidity rises above eighty, temperature increases by two and yeast gas concentration goes up by five. To prevent overproofing, if gas concentration exceeds twenty, the fan speed sets to high, dropping humidity by ten and gas concentration to zero. Return the final humidity, internal temperature, and fan speed.

title: Particle Detector Calorimeter
spec: Implement a class tracking a high energy physics calorimeter. The entry function `detect(events)` takes a list of integers representing particle energy deposits. The system monitors total absorbed energy starting at zero, trigger rate starting at zero, cooling flow starting at base level, and sensor bias voltage starting at one hundred. Each event adds to absorbed energy and increments the trigger rate. If five consecutive events occur, cooling flow switches to maximum to prevent thermal noise. If a massive deposit over one thousand is detected, the sensor overloads, dropping bias voltage to zero, and the system ignores events until a reset command string is given. Return the total absorbed energy, final bias voltage, and cooling flow state.

title: Automatic Tire Inflation System
spec: Create a class managing a dynamic tire pressure system. The entry function `inflate(changes)` receives a list of string conditions. The system tracks current pressure starting at thirty five, target pressure starting at thirty five, compressor load starting at zero, and release valve status starting at closed. A highway condition sets target pressure to forty; sand sets it to twenty; mud sets it to twenty five. The system adjusts current pressure by five units per step towards the target. Pumping increases compressor load by ten per step. Releasing air opens the valve and resets compressor load to zero. If load exceeds fifty, a cooldown cycle pauses inflation for one step. Return the final current pressure, compressor load, and valve status.

title: Wind Tunnel Airflow Modulator
spec: Design a class for a supersonic wind tunnel. The function `modulate(commands)` processes a list of string commands. The tunnel tracks main fan pitch starting at zero, air velocity starting at zero, turbulence grid status starting at retracted, and test section pressure starting at one hundred. A spool command increases fan pitch by ten and velocity by fifty. A choke command drops test section pressure by twenty to simulate high altitude. If velocity exceeds two hundred, the turbulence grid must be deployed automatically, which drops velocity by twenty but increases pressure by ten. A vent command resets velocity to zero and retracts the grid. Return the final fan pitch, air velocity, and turbulence grid status.

title: Automated Bowling Alley Pinsetter
spec: Write a class simulating a pinsetter machine. The entry function `bowl(rolls)` takes a list of integers representing pins knocked down. The machine tracks standing pins starting at ten, sweep bar position starting at up, table height starting at high, and ball return mechanism status starting at idle. For each roll, standing pins are reduced. The sweep bar drops to clear dead wood, triggering the ball return to active. If standing pins reach zero, the table lowers to place a new set of ten pins, and the sweep bar returns up. If a foul string is encountered, the sweep bar immediately resets all ten pins regardless of the roll, and the return mechanism jams until a reset string is provided. Return the final standing pins, sweep bar position, and table height.

title: Tunnel Boring Machine Operator
spec: Implement a class for a tunnel boring machine. The entry function `bore(strata)` processes a list of strings representing rock types. The machine tracks thrust cylinder pressure starting at five hundred, cutterhead speed starting at ten, muck removal rate starting at zero, and shield position starting at zero. Soft dirt increases muck rate by twenty and advances the shield by two. Hard rock decreases cutterhead speed by three and increases thrust pressure by one hundred to advance the shield by one. If thrust pressure exceeds eight hundred, an overload occurs, stopping the cutterhead and setting muck rate to zero. A maintenance string restores speed and pressure to default values. Return the final thrust pressure, cutterhead speed, and total shield advance.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanner
spec: Create a class for an MRI machine controller. The function `scan(sequences)` accepts a list of integers representing radio frequency pulse durations. The scanner maintains magnetic field strength starting at one, gradient coil temperature starting at twenty, helium level starting at one hundred, and image resolution starting at zero. Each pulse adds to the image resolution but increases coil temperature by half the pulse duration. If temperature exceeds eighty, helium level drops by ten to cool the coils back to forty. If helium level falls below twenty, the magnetic field quenches, dropping strength to zero and halting all further scans to prevent catastrophic failure. Return the final image resolution, coil temperature, and helium level.

title: Geothermal Power Plant Turbine
spec: Write a class to govern a geothermal steam turbine. The entry function `generate(pressures)` receives a list of integers representing incoming steam pressure surges. The plant tracks internal steam pressure starting at fifty, rotor revolutions starting at three thousand, generator output starting at one hundred, and vibration frequency starting at ten. A surge adds to internal pressure and increases rotor revolutions by fifty times the surge. Generator output scales with revolutions. However, if revolutions exceed four thousand, vibration frequency doubles. A vibration over fifty triggers a bypass valve, venting steam, dropping internal pressure to ten, and halving revolutions. Return the final generator output, internal pressure, and vibration frequency.

title: Industrial Meat Slicer Controller
spec: Develop a class for an automated meat deli slicer. The entry function `slice(requests)` takes a list of string thickness settings. The slicer monitors blade speed starting at zero, carriage tempo starting at zero, slice count starting at zero, and safety guard lock starting as engaged. A power on string sets blade speed to high and carriage tempo to medium. A thick request produces one slice but slows the carriage tempo. A thin request produces two slices and increases carriage tempo. If the requested setting changes three times in a row, the motor overheats, dropping blade speed to zero and disengaging the safety lock. Return the total slice count, blade speed, and safety guard lock status.

title: Passenger Airplane Flap Actuator
spec: Implement a class for an aircraft trailing edge flap system. The function `adjust(airspeeds)` processes a list of integers. The system tracks flap angle starting at zero, left hydraulic pressure starting at full, right hydraulic pressure starting at full, and asymmetry lock starting at false. As airspeed drops below two hundred, flap angle increases by ten for every twenty unit drop. Extending flaps consumes hydraulic pressure equally. If left and right pressures differ by more than ten, the asymmetry lock engages, freezing the flap angle to prevent structural twisting. A pump command string equalizes and refills both pressures. Return the final flap angle, left hydraulic pressure, and asymmetry lock status.

title: Concert Stage Lighting Rig
spec: Design a class for an intelligent moving head light. The entry function `illuminate(cues)` accepts a list of string color commands. The rig tracks pan angle starting at center, tilt angle starting at level, color wheel position starting at white, and shutter status starting at open. A red cue shifts the color wheel and pans left by ten degrees. A blue cue shifts the color wheel and tilts up by fifteen degrees. A blackout cue snaps the shutter to closed and resets pan and tilt. If the pan angle goes beyond fifty degrees from center, a limit switch triggers, forcing the shutter closed and freezing motion until a home cue is received. Return the final pan angle, tilt angle, and shutter status.

title: Robotic Surgical Arm Calibrator
spec: Write a class for a micro surgery robotic arm. The entry function `operate(movements)` takes a list of integers representing millimeter shifts. The arm maintains absolute x position starting at zero, absolute y position starting at zero, force feedback threshold starting at low, and safety clamp status starting at open. Positive shifts add to x, negative shifts subtract from y. If a single shift exceeds ten millimeters, the movement is considered erratic: the safety clamp closes instantly, and force feedback threshold switches to high. While the clamp is closed, all subsequent movements are ignored until an unlock string is processed. Return the final x position, y position, and clamp status.

title: Mechanical Metronome Tracker
spec: Model a mechanical metronome that maintains its internal state. It tracks spring tension starting at zero, swing amplitude starting at twenty, and a direction multiplier starting at one. The entry function `simulate(commands)` processes a list of numbers and strings. A number adds to the tension, capping at one hundred. A string command is the word tick. During a tick, a baseline friction reduces tension by one. Then, if tension remains strictly positive, tension decreases by three and amplitude increases by two, capped at forty. If tension is zero or less, amplitude decreases by four, with a minimum of zero. After these adjustments, the direction multiplier changes sign, and the current position is recorded as the product of direction and amplitude. Return a list of positions recorded at each tick. Example: input of ten, the string tick, and the string tick outputs negative twenty two and twenty four.

title: Mine Cart Brake System
spec: Model a stateful mine cart navigating a steep track. The cart maintains speed starting at zero, brake pad thickness starting at one hundred, and shoe heat starting at zero. The entry function `descend(segments)` processes a list of track slope numbers. For each slope, the cart speed increases by the slope value. If the speed exceeds twenty, the brakes automatically engage. Engaging brakes reduces speed by ten, reduces brake pad thickness by two, and increases shoe heat by fifteen. If shoe heat exceeds fifty, the brake effectiveness drops, reducing speed by only five instead of ten, while still consuming the pad and adding heat. If the pad thickness reaches zero, brakes fail and cannot engage. Return a list of speeds at the end of each track segment. Example: input of five, twenty, and fifteen outputs five, fifteen, and twenty.

title: Waterwheel Mill Operator
spec: Model a stateful waterwheel that drives a grinding stone. The wheel maintains water momentum starting at zero, stone rotation speed starting at zero, and flour produced starting at zero. The entry function `grind(flows)` receives a list of water flow rates. For each flow rate, momentum increases by the flow and then decreases by a natural drag of two, down to a minimum of zero. The stone speed adjusts to match half of the current momentum, rounded down. If the stone speed is above five, it produces flour equal to the stone speed minus five, adding to the total. After processing all flows, return the total flour produced and the final stone speed as a tuple. Example: input of ten, fifteen, and zero outputs a tuple of ten and four.

title: Funicular Rail Ascender
spec: Model a stateful funicular rail ascender mechanism. It tracks grip tension starting at zero, jaw wear starting at zero, and carriage speed starting at zero. The entry function `operate(actions)` takes a list of strings: tighten, loosen, or coast. The string tighten increases grip tension by five. The string loosen decreases it by five. Coasting applies track friction. When tension is above ten, the jaw wear increases by one per action and carriage speed increases by two up to a maximum of twenty. When tension is ten or below, speed decreases by three per action due to friction, down to zero. If jaw wear exceeds twenty, tightening only increases tension by three. Return the final speed and jaw wear as a tuple after processing the sequence. Example: input of seven tightens and three coasts outputs twenty and ten.

title: Parachute Deployment Tracker
spec: Model a stateful skydiver and parachute system. It tracks altitude starting at ten thousand, freefall speed starting at zero, and canopy spread percent starting at zero. The entry function `descend(actions)` processes a list where each element is either a number of seconds to fall, or the string pull. For a number of seconds, altitude drops by the speed multiplied by seconds, while speed increases by ten every second up to a terminal velocity of one hundred twenty. If the string pull is encountered, the canopy spread increases by twenty percent per second in subsequent falls. The terminal velocity decreases by one for every percent of canopy spread. Return the altitude when it reaches zero or below, or the final altitude if the sequence ends before reaching the ground. Example: input of ten, the string pull, and five outputs eight thousand eight hundred.

title: Windmill Grindstone Controller
spec: Model a stateful windmill adjusting to wind conditions. It maintains blade pitch angle starting at zero, wind efficiency starting at ten, and structural stress starting at zero. The entry function `process(gusts)` takes a list of wind speeds. For each wind speed, if it exceeds fifty, the pitch angle increases by five to spill wind, and structural stress increases by the speed minus fifty. If the wind speed is below twenty, the pitch angle decreases by two to catch more wind, bounded at a minimum of zero. Wind efficiency is calculated as one hundred minus the pitch angle. Return a list of wind efficiencies after each gust. Example: input of sixty, fifteen, and seventy outputs ninety, ninety two, and eighty two.

title: Trebuchet Launch Calculator
spec: Model a stateful siege trebuchet preparing for launch. It tracks counterweight mass starting at five hundred, sling length starting at ten, and beam pivot stress starting at zero. The entry function `launch(adjustments)` takes a list of numbers representing payload weights. For each payload, the mechanism attempts a test swing. The swing generates pivot stress equal to the payload weight multiplied by the sling length, divided by ten. If this stress exceeds the counterweight mass, the swing fails and sling length is reduced by one to compensate for the next attempt. Otherwise, the swing succeeds and counterweight mass drops by five due to lost ballast. Return the number of successful swings. Example: input of three hundred, six hundred, and four hundred outputs two.

title: Crossbow Tension Tracker
spec: Model a stateful heavy crossbow mechanism. It maintains bowstring draw distance starting at zero, material fatigue starting at zero, and stored energy starting at zero. The entry function `fire(cranks)` takes a list of integers representing turns of the winding winch. Each turn increases the draw distance by two and the stored energy by the current draw distance. However, every turn also adds one to material fatigue. If material fatigue reaches ten, subsequent turns only increase draw distance by one and add no stored energy due to micro fractures in the prod. Return a list of stored energy values after each set of winch turns is fully applied. Example: input containing three and then two outputs twelve and thirty two.

title: Steamboat Paddlewheel
spec: Model a stateful river steamboat paddlewheel. It tracks boiler pressure starting at fifty, paddle depth starting at five, and distance traveled starting at zero. The entry function `navigate(commands)` takes a list of strings: either stoke or paddle. The string stoke increases boiler pressure by twenty. The string paddle consumes ten boiler pressure to rotate the wheel, moving the boat forward by a distance equal to the paddle depth. If boiler pressure falls below ten, paddle commands have no effect. If boiler pressure exceeds one hundred, the safety valve vents, reducing pressure to fifty and reducing paddle depth by one due to the jarring vibration. Return the total distance traveled after all commands. Example: input of stoke, paddle, and paddle outputs ten.

title: Rowboat Oar Synchronizer
spec: Model a stateful rowboat maintaining a straight course. It tracks heading angle starting at zero, left side momentum starting at zero, and right side momentum starting at zero. The entry function `row(strokes)` takes a list of pairs, where each pair contains the left oar force and right oar force. For each stroke, the left momentum increases by the left force and right momentum by the right force. Both momentums then decay by ten percent, rounded down. The heading angle changes by the difference between right and left momentum. Return a list of heading angles after each stroke.
